decisions.reason: As a newly launched safety-shoe line in the firm’s core category, it is likely to be retained because a large established producer with organisational slack will usually give such models more time unless results clearly fall below aspirations.

The comfort insole is complementary to the core footwear business and supports cross-selling, so management would likely keep it for now, though its lower strategic prominence makes it somewhat more droppable if performance disappoints.

The supportive insole fits the existing product system and customer needs, but because it is an accessory with possible overlap with other insoles, it faces a somewhat higher chance of being dropped if it underperforms aspiration levels.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series with its own page signals managerial attention and commitment, so under the behavioral view it would likely be protected and given time to prove itself.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a relevant but more specialized extension of the firm’s protective-footwear capabilities, so they are likely to stay unless niche demand falls clearly short of expectations.

Because the moulded insole was presented as a flagship direction and shown on the home page, management would be very unlikely to withdraw it quickly and would instead continue backing it as part of the firm’s innovation path.
